description:
Enum over a JSON-decoded value fails: Enum.count(Json.decode!("[1]")) -> artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan, Enumerable.count/1 has no implementation.

Root cause (reader 2026-10-17): protocol dispatch on an any receiver already works (resolve_protocol_call, src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:~1560-1710, keeps every overlapping impl; call_destinations builds a runtime PatternDispatchPlan). Enumerable.count(d) called directly works. The failure is contract refinement: Enum.count's @spec count(Enumerable.t(a)) (lib/enum.fz:109). refine_contract_inputs (semantic.rs:2162-2190) narrows each input to intersect(input, spec param); for any that yields the ProtocolDomain opaque marker (Types::protocol_domain_of, types/mod.rs:1360), which overlaps no impl target. Concrete receivers survive only because their intersection is empty and the fallback keeps the original.

Probes: a no-@spec wrapper works; the same wrapper with @spec c(Enumerable.t(a)) fails; a user protocol with @spec c(Sz.t(a)) fails on any and works on [1].
title: Enum and protocol dispatch work on runtime-typed values
